body:
Short answer: the current RecallSegmenter is not innovative and not state of the art. It is useful scaffolding. The library as a whole is not yet a SOTA empirical system because it has not entered or beaten a relevant benchmark.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS

1. Modern discourse segmentation is a mature benchmarked task. DISRPT covers 24 corpora, 13 languages, multiple discourse frameworks, and reports state-of-the-art multilingual systems. Its 2024 paper says segmentation performance is approaching a plateau, while connective and relation classification remain harder:
https://aclanthology.org/2024.lrec-main.447/

2. Automatic event segmentation plus automatic narrative-recall scoring already exists. Panela et al. use GPT-4 and LLaMA for event boundaries, then USE, OpenAI, LaBSE, and MPNet embeddings to score spoken recall, with human validation:
https://www.nature.com/articles/s44271-025-00359-7

3. Data-driven probabilistic and hierarchical event segmentation in narrative perception and recall is not new. Baldassano et al. use an HMM to discover nested event structure and relate it to later free recall:
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5558154/

4. Automated Autobiographical Interview scoring is already published. van Genugten and Schacter fine-tune DistilBERT across five datasets; later work reports LLaMA-3 scores approaching human-rater agreement:
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10990986/
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40750940/

5. Joint event coreference, temporal, causal, and subevent extraction is also an established research programme; MAVEN-ERE supplies a large unified benchmark and shows joint learning helps:
https://aclanthology.org/2022.emnlp-main.60/

So these claims would be false today:
- "We invented automatic recall segmentation."
- "We invented event-based recall scoring."
- "Using an LLM or embeddings makes this SOTA."
- "A partial alignment architecture is SOTA because it is sophisticated."

WHAT MAY BE INNOVATIVE

I did not find, in this bounded primary-source search, an end-to-end system that combines all of these:

- exact source-span evidence and construction receipts;
- separate uncertainty for segmentation, propositions, entities, coreference, temporal and causal claims;
- retained alternative unitizations or Unresolved outcomes;
- partial, unbalanced, hierarchical alignment with explicit external destinations;
- separate discourse, story-world, and recall clocks;
- role, polarity, context, modality, and relation fidelity rather than one semantic score;
- propagation of construction uncertainty into recall signatures and population estimands;
- a prohibition on silently turning missing support into a numeric value.

That combination is a plausible research contribution. It is not yet an established novelty claim. A systematic review could still find adjacent systems, and an architecture is not SOTA until measured.

WHAT WE ARE DOING HERE

We should be building the scientific instrument that the current literature mostly does not provide: one that can say exactly what analysis was run, what choices it conditioned on, what evidence licensed them, which alternatives survived, and how conclusions change under another admissible construction.

That has two deliverables:

A. Engineering contribution: a portable, auditable contract that can admit existing or future SOTA providers without letting their guesses become facts.

B. Scientific contribution: evidence that segmentation and interpretation uncertainty materially alter recall conclusions, and a method that carries that uncertainty more faithfully than fixed-boundary embedding scores.

THE BAR

Before using SOTA or innovative in public, run a real court:

1. Benchmark boundary detection against DISRPT-style segmenters, the Panela LLM method, the current rule baseline, and independently adjudicated recall boundaries.
2. Benchmark relation and coreference channels against appropriate published baselines rather than judging the whole graph by one score.
3. Compare fixed segmentation, retained-alternative sensitivity, and any later ensemble on held-out stories.
4. Measure calibration, coverage, abstention, cross-story generalization, and downstream conclusion stability.
5. Compare directly with event-level embedding recall scoring and automated AI scoring.
6. Show an ablation: the uncertainty machinery changes or improves a scientific conclusion. If it never matters, it is elaborate record-keeping, not a scientific advance.

My recommendation: call storymodel4s an auditable research platform aimed at an open integration and estimand problem. Do not call it SOTA yet. Keep the regex segmenter as a named baseline. The innovative wager is uncertainty-preserving Narrative Process Alignment; the next programme must test that wager hard enough to lose.

This is a bounded primary-source assessment, not a systematic review and not a novelty certification. No implementation or scope authority claimed.
